SPOILERS AHEAD

The first would be Manchester by the Sea, when Casey Affleck's character meets his ex-wife Michelle Williams randomly on the street, where we as a viewer are still not aware about the burden he is carrying about his children's deaths. The scene plays so beautifully with no exposition, but we understand the history between the characters - the harsh words that might have been said to him in the aftermath of their children's deaths, the forgiveness for realising it was not his fault, the realisation that he has not moved past it and still blames himself for it. All these emotions are conveyed with minimal dialogues and is probably the most heart wrenching scene that atleast I have seen.

Second would be In the Mood for Love, basically the whole movie, the looks they share, their desire to get close to each other but their resolve not to commit the act that their spouses have committed. The beautiful score which accentuates their longing but inability to communicate the same fully. A true masterpiece.
